inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 10-K (period ended 2026-01-31): StockBasedComp cash-flow add-back $788M + taxes paid related to net share settlement of equity awards (financing activities) $289M = $1,077M combined; Autodesk publishes no single combined line, so the two are summed per method section 1(a) fallback. H1 FY2027 run-rate (Q2 FY2027 10-Q): SBC $339M + net-settlement taxes $157M = $496M on $3,980M revenue = 12.5%, which is what the forward sbc_pct_path is anchored to.
inputs.balance_sheet_date: 2026-07-31 (Q2 FY2027 10-Q, the latest filed balance sheet; Q3 FY2027 is due 2026-11-24), adjusted pro-forma for the MaintainX close on 2026-08-03 using the 10-Q's own Note 11 and Note 19. Cash and securities at 31 July: cash $4,098M + short-term marketable securities $57M + long-term marketable securities $202M = $4,357M, plus the $1,000M 364-day term loan drawn on 3 August, less $3,530M preliminary purchase consideration net of cash acquired = $1,827M pro-forma. Debt: $2,500M senior notes (principal) + $1,000M commercial paper already outstanding at 31 July + $1,000M term loan = $4,500M. Pro-forma net debt $2,673M. CORRECTION to the 2026-09-25 version, which carried net debt of $2M: it assumed only $1.6B of cash left the business and that debt stayed at $2,500M, missing both the commercial paper and the term loan that the 10-Q states financed the deal.
inputs.share_count_date: 2026-07-31 (Q2 FY2027 10-Q, weighted-average diluted shares for the quarter, 211M; 4M shares were repurchased for $901M in H1 FY2027)
inputs.share_count_basis: fully diluted weighted average, Q2 FY2027 10-Q; held FLAT because SBC and net-settlement taxes are fully expensed in the flows, and FY2026 buybacks of $1,402M ($901M in H1 FY2027) are the cash mechanism actually funding that flat count
inputs.wacc_rationale: 9.0% base for a large-cap US software company: ~4.1% risk-free (10Y UST), ~5.5% ERP, beta ~1.05-1.1 reflecting moderate cyclicality in AEC/manufacturing capex exposure. USD flows, USD rate. Leverage is now modest rather than nil (pro-forma net debt ~0.9x pre-SBC EBITDA, $2.0B of it short-dated commercial paper and a 364-day term loan that must be refinanced or repaid from FCF within a year). Per-scenario WACC (bull 8.5 / base 9.0 / bear 10.0) is carried UNCHANGED from the prior version so the update stays comparable; note the house rule that risk should be charged once argues for a single 9% across scenarios, which would raise bear and lower bull -- left for the user to decide rather than changed silently.
inputs.lease_treatment: not material - Autodesk's operating leases are small (office space); no separate lease line modelled, consistent with a software cost structure with capex <1% of revenue
inputs.nci_treatment: none - wholly owned, no minority interests
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF DCF (component build), routed via .claude/skills/dcf-methods/SKILL.md as a SaaS/software operating company; same model as the 2026-09-25 version. This is an UPDATE with two error corrections and two driver re-anchors -- see reconciliation. (1) NET DEBT corrected from ~$0 to $2,673M pro-forma: the MaintainX deal ($3.53B net of cash acquired, closed 2026-08-03) was financed with $1.0B commercial paper, a $1.0B 364-day term loan and cash on hand, per the Q2 FY2027 10-Q. (2) EBITDA MARGIN BASIS corrected: the engine's ebitda_margin_path is a PRE-SBC margin from which sbc_pct_path is then deducted, but the prior version fed it the GAAP EBITDA margin (FY2026 $1,773M = GAAP operating income $1,578M + D&A, 24.6%), which is already after $788M of SBC expense. SBC was therefore charged twice: the prior base year-1 owner FCF was $920M (11.1% margin) against FY2026 actual owner FCF of $1,332M (18.5%) and ~$1,650M implied by FY2027 FCF guidance. Margins are now stated pre-SBC and year 1 is calibrated so the component build reproduces FY2027 guidance: reported FCF guide $2,725-2,750M less SBC+net-settlement taxes at 13.0% of $8,323M revenue = ~$1,655M levered owner FCF, ~$1,685M unlevered. That calibration gives a 35.0% pre-SBC EBITDA margin, deliberately below the H1 FY2027 actual of 39.7% (GAAP operating income $1,140M + D&A $101M + SBC $339M on $3,980M) because H2 absorbs MaintainX integration cost, seasonally heavier cash tax and deal costs that guidance already nets out; if H2 holds nearer the H1 margin the model is conservative in year 1. Fiscal year ends Jan 31; 'FY2026' = year ended 2026-01-31 (latest completed FY), FY2027 is forecast year 1 with H1 actual and Q3 complete but unreported. Interest income IS disclosed ($83M FY2026; $52M H1 FY2027, against $44M interest expense) -- the prior note saying otherwise was wrong -- but it is not stripped: the company is in a net DEBT position, so there is no cash pile being double-counted, and forward flows are built unlevered from components. Share count held FLAT (211M) because SBC is fully expensed in the flows. MaintainX's ~$60M H2 FY2027 revenue is inside the guidance-based year-1 growth rate; no separate segment DCF (it is ~0.7% of guided revenue), which may understate its medium-term contribution to the Operations pillar. The $150M of restricted stock issued to MaintainX employees is treated as retention compensation and is why year-1 SBC is set at 13.0% rather than the 12.5% H1 run-rate. Price is a regular-session close, not an after-hours print. Q3 FY2027 results on 2026-11-24 will replace the pro-forma balance sheet and the year-1 anchors within days of this valuation.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (25.8-38.5%) is a large positive outlier vs revenue/FCF CAGRs and is NOT used as the growth proxy: Autodesk ran negative/near-zero shareholders' equity from FY2017-FY2020 (aggressive buybacks exceeding retained earnings), so the equity base-year denominator is depressed and the resulting 'CAGR' overstates true compounding -- it is a capital-structure artifact, not a growth signal. Revenue 3yr CAGR (12.9%) is used as the anchor instead, corroborated by owner-FCF 5yr CAGR of 11.0% and the FY2027 guided growth of ~15.5%. EPS 5yr CAGR is negative only because FY2021 EPS ($5.44) included a one-off tax benefit spike -- not a growth signal either; EPS 3yr CAGR (11.4%) off a cleaner base is consistent with revenue growth.
historical_growth.notes: Unchanged from the prior version: FY0 is still FY2026 and no annual period has been added. FY2026 and FY2027 reported revenue growth (17.5%, ~15.5% guided) both carry a gross-up tailwind from the new transaction model (direct revenue $2,563M -> $4,560M in FY2026) and FY2027 adds ~0.7pt from MaintainX; current RPO grew ~12% year on year at Q2 FY2027 ($5,240M vs $4,680M), a better read of underlying growth than reported revenue.

base.ebitda_margin_note: PRE-SBC EBITDA margin (GAAP operating income + D&A + SBC expense). FY2026 actual 35.5%; H1 FY2027 actual 39.7%; year 1 calibrated to FY2027 FCF guidance. +3pp expansion to a 38% steady state by year 7.
base.sbc_pct_note: SBC expense plus cash taxes on net share settlement, % of revenue. FY2026 14.9%; H1 FY2027 12.5%; year 1 at 13.0% to carry the MaintainX retention stock. Year-10 endpoint (9.3%) unchanged from the prior version.
base.narrative: Base case: FY2027 revenue lands at the midpoint of raised guidance (~15.5%, including ~$60M of H2 MaintainX), then decelerates as the transaction-model gross-up rolls off, the AEC/manufacturing installed base matures and price-increase headroom narrows, settling near 6% by year 10. Seat counts hold: AI features are monetised as consumption on top of the named-user seat, as management describes, without becoming a new growth leg. Pre-SBC EBITDA margin starts at 35.0% -- the level at which the component build reproduces FY2027 free-cash-flow guidance -- and expands 3pp to 38% as sales-and-marketing optimisation after the agency-model transition and MaintainX integration costs roll off. SBC plus net-settlement taxes fade from 13.0% of revenue toward ~9% as the revenue base outgrows grants. Cash tax rate ramps from its recent trough (FY2026 cash taxes $258M) toward a ~23% normalised blended global rate.

bull.ebitda_margin_note: PRE-SBC basis, as base. Reaches 40%, in line with the H1 FY2027 actual (39.7%) being sustained once integration costs clear.
bull.narrative: Bull case: the agentic-AI question resolves in Autodesk's favour -- agents need a licensed named-user seat to orchestrate them, so AI adds a consumption/token revenue layer (Autodesk AI in Fusion, Forma, AutoCAD) on top of an intact seat base rather than shrinking it. Construction sustains 20%+ growth for longer, and MaintainX integrates quickly enough to make 'Design, Make, Operate' a durable third growth vector. FY2027 finishes just above the top of guidance (16%), growth holds in the mid-teens for two more years, and the H1 FY2027 pre-SBC EBITDA margin of ~40% proves sustainable as sales-and-marketing efficiency from the completed agency model compounds. Requires several independent things to go right (AI monetisation without seat loss, MaintainX integration, sustained construction growth, no share loss to Procore/Dassault).

bear.ebitda_margin_note: PRE-SBC basis, as base. Ends 5pp below base, the same gap as the prior version.
bear.narrative: Bear case: the fear that drove the 2026 de-rating turns out to be right. AI-augmented design workflows let architecture, engineering and manufacturing firms deliver the same output with fewer licensed seats; seat counts start to shrink at renewal from FY2028, and consumption pricing recovers only part of the lost seat revenue. That lands on top of European/APAC macro softness and AEC/manufacturing capex cyclicality, with Dassault/Siemens/PTC taking share in manufacturing/PLM and Procore/Trimble capping construction. FY2027 itself still lands at the bottom of guidance (15%) because nine months are already in, but growth drops to 8% in FY2028 and to 3-5% thereafter. MaintainX integration proves costly and distracting under a new AEC leader, the $2.0B of short-dated acquisition debt absorbs cash that would otherwise fund buybacks, and the pre-SBC EBITDA margin slips from 34% to 33% instead of expanding. SBC stays elevated as retention grants are needed to hold engineering talent against AI-native competitors.

scenario_narratives.base: FY2027 at the guidance midpoint (~15.5%), decelerating to 6% by year 10 with seat counts intact and AI monetised as add-on consumption; pre-SBC EBITDA margin expands from 35% (calibrated to FY2027 FCF guidance) to 38%; SBC plus net-settlement taxes fade from 13% toward ~9% of revenue.
scenario_narratives.bull: Agentic AI adds a consumption layer on top of an intact seat base, construction sustains 20%+ growth and MaintainX makes 'Operate' a third growth vector; mid-teens growth for three years and a 40% pre-SBC EBITDA margin, in line with the H1 FY2027 actual. Needs several independent execution wins.
scenario_narratives.bear: AI-augmented workflows shrink licensed seat counts from FY2028 while macro softness and competition (Dassault/Siemens/PTC, Procore/Trimble) compound it; growth falls to 8% then 3-5%, MaintainX integration and its short-dated debt weigh, and the pre-SBC EBITDA margin drifts down to 33%.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: UNCHANGED at 20/50/30, deliberately. Bear stays at 20% (above the 15% house default): the agentic-AI threat to seat licensing is now the named bear axis, but there is still no evidence of it in reported numbers -- Q2 FY2027 was a beat-and-raise, current RPO grew ~12% and management reports no seat erosion -- and the share-price falls since September are sector sentiment, not company data, so they are not a reason to move a probability. The MaintainX integration load, $2.0B of short-dated acquisition debt and an AEC leadership handover keep it above default. Base at 50% is the guidance-consistent path. Bull stays trimmed to 30% because it needs several independent things to go right (AI monetisation without seat loss, MaintainX integration, sustained 20%+ construction growth, no share loss). What would move these: Q3 FY2027 results on 2026-11-24 -- a decline in net revenue retention or seat counts, or a cut to FY2027 billings guidance, would take bear to 30%; a second consecutive raise with stable retention and visible AI consumption revenue would restore the 15/50/35 default.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Autodesk is a high-quality, ~97%-recurring-revenue software platform with a dominant, hard-to-displace position in AEC/BIM (AutoCAD, Revit, the DWG file-format standard) and a leading-but-more-contested position in manufacturing/PLM. The investment case rests on continued margin expansion now that the multi-year transaction-model transition is complete, secular digitisation tailwinds, and the MaintainX-enabled expansion into building/asset operations -- set against the open question of whether agentic AI erodes per-seat licensing. The owner-FCF DCF (component build, 10-year horizon) values the business on cash available to shareholders after fully charging stock-based compensation and the cash taxes paid on net share settlement, which together run 12.5-15% of revenue and are the largest swing factor between the house and street values.
key_risks_to_valuation: Agentic AI and seat-based licensing: the bear case has seat counts shrinking from FY2028 and is worth well under half the base value per share; nothing in reported results confirms or refutes it yet, and Q3 FY2027 on 2026-11-24 is the next data point

Year-1 anchors are pro-forma and guidance-based: net debt is built from the 31 July 2026 balance sheet plus the disclosed MaintainX financing, and the year-1 margin is calibrated to FY2027 FCF guidance rather than to an actual; both are superseded when the Q3 FY2027 10-Q is filed

MaintainX integration risk -- the largest acquisition in company history ($3.53B net of cash acquired), financed with $2.0B of commercial paper and a 364-day term loan that must be refinanced or repaid within a year
SBC plus net-settlement taxes are assumed to decline from 13% to ~9% of revenue over 10 years; if competition for engineering talent keeps grants elevated, the house value is overstated
Cyclical AEC/manufacturing capex exposure -- a macro slowdown (flagged specifically for Europe/APAC) would compress new-seat growth and EBA renewals

Reported growth in FY2026-FY2027 is flattered by the transaction-model gross-up; current RPO growth (~12%) is below reported revenue growth (~16%), so the step down to 13.5% in year 2 may still be generous
Terminal value is Gordon-bound in all three scenarios (below the cap) and is the majority of enterprise value given the 10-year horizon -- see terminal_pct_of_value per scenario
unchanged_assumptions: Growth paths for years 2-10 in all three scenarios: no new operating data since the Q2 FY2027 10-Q. Would move on Q3 FY2027 results, the FY2028 guide in February 2027, or disclosed seat/net-revenue-retention trends.

D&A, capex, cash-tax and working-capital-capture paths: unchanged. The D&A path would move once MaintainX purchase accounting is disclosed (intangible amortisation is non-cash and only affects the tax shield here); the cash-tax path would move on the FY2027 10-K cash-taxes-paid figure.
WACC, terminal growth and terminal cap multiples, including the per-scenario WACC spread: unchanged; see wacc_rationale.
Share count 211M and the FY2026 owner-FCF base (last_fcf $1,332M): unchanged; no newer filing exists.
